amt_statutory_rates.title: IRC § 55 — Alternative Minimum Tax (26%/28% rates; 25% exemption phase-out, pre-OBBBA)
amt_statutory_rates.note: § 55(b)(1)(A): tentative minimum tax is 26% of the taxable excess up to the inflation-indexed 28% breakpoint plus 28% above it (MFS breakpoint is half). § 55(d)(2): the exemption is reduced by 25% of AMTI over the phase-out threshold — in effect for 2023-2025. § 55(d)(3) is the inflation-adjustment mechanism for the breakpoint, exemption and phase-out threshold (rounded to $100). The 26%/28% rates themselves are statutory and not indexed. The 50% phase-out rate for 2026 is OBBBA §70107 (see obbba_amt_2026).

cfr_1010_821_fbar_penalties.title: 31 CFR 1010.821 — Penalty adjustment and table (FinCEN civil monetary penalty inflation adjustment)
cfr_1010_821_fbar_penalties.quote: Maximum penalty amounts or range of minimum and maximum penalty amounts for penalties assessed on or after January 17, 2025
cfr_1010_821_fbar_penalties.note: 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(B)(i) Foreign Financial Agency Transaction — Non-Willful Violation: adjusted maximum $16,536. 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(C)(i)(I) Willful Violation: adjusted maximum $165,353 (the willful penalty is the GREATER of that figure or 50% of the account balance at the time of the violation, per 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(D)(ii)). The statutory bases are $10,000 and $100,000; the table figures are those bases inflation-adjusted under the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act. Keyed by ASSESSMENT date, not tax year. Bittner v. United States, 598 U.S. 85 (2023) fixed the non-willful penalty as per report, not per account (fbar.penalty_unit).

irs_fbar_requirements.title: IRS — Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
irs_fbar_requirements.note: Filing required when the aggregate value of all foreign financial accounts EXCEEDED $10,000 at any time during the calendar year (measured on each account's maximum value, not its year-end balance) — hence threshold_test 'exceeds': exactly $10,000 does not trigger. Due April 15 of the following year with an AUTOMATIC extension to October 15 (no request required). Records — name on the account, account number, name and address of the institution, type of account, maximum value — must be kept for five years from the FBAR due date. Whether the account produced taxable income is irrelevant.

fincen_maximum_account_value.title: FinCEN — Reporting Maximum Account Value
fincen_maximum_account_value.note: Periodic account statements may be relied on to determine the maximum value, provided they fairly reflect the maximum account value during the calendar year. Non-USD amounts are converted using the Treasury Reporting Rate of Exchange for the LAST DAY OF THE CALENDAR YEAR — not the rate on the date the account peaked, and not a commercial mid-market rate. Where the maximum cannot be determined and the filer has fewer than 25 accounts, complete the other fields and check the Item 15a 'amount unknown' box.

irm_4_26_16_fbar.title: IRM 4.26.16 — Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
irm_4_26_16_fbar.note: Items 14a/14b: a filer with 25 or more accounts reports the number of accounts and does not complete the per-account Parts II–V, but must retain the detail records and furnish them on request. The Item 15a 'amount unknown' election is available to filers with FEWER than 25 accounts.

ftc_904j.title: IRS Instructions for Form 1116 — IRC 904(j) election to claim the FTC without Form 1116
ftc_904j.note: IRC 904(j) election: a taxpayer may claim the foreign tax credit directly on Schedule 3 (Form 1040), Part I, line 1 without filing Form 1116 when (1) ALL foreign-source gross income is passive-category income, (2) it was reported on a qualified payee statement (1099-DIV Box 7, 1099-INT Box 6, K-1/K-3, etc.), and (3) total creditable foreign taxes are $300 or less ($600 if MFJ). Not available to estates/trusts. The election permanently forfeits FTC carryback/carryforward for that year. $300/$600 limits are statutory and not inflation-indexed, so one shared block serves every year.

obbba_energy_terminations.title: IRS FAQs — modification of §§25C/25D/25E/30D/45W under Public Law 119-21 (OBBBA)

L. 119-21) terminated the clean-energy credits on an accelerated schedule: §§30D/25E/45W — no credit for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30 ('acquired' = written binding contract + payment, incl. a nominal down payment or trade-in, on or before that date); §25C — property placed in service after 2025-12-31; §25D — expenditures made after 2025-12-31. 2023 and 2024 blocks carry NO terminated_after key (credits ran all year pre-OBBBA); 2026 has no energy_credits block at all. irc_168k_bonus.title: 26 USC 168(k) (bonus depreciation), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 (OBBBA)
irc_168k_bonus.note: Pre-OBBBA TCJA phasedown (former 168(k)(6)(A)): 80% (2023), 60% (2024), 40% (2025). OBBBA (Pub. L. 119-21, enacted 2025-07-04) restored 100% as the default in 168(k)(1)(A) for property acquired after Jan 19, 2025 and placed in service after that date; property acquired on/before Jan 19, 2025 keeps the pre-OBBBA schedule (40% for 2025). A 168(k)(10) transition election allows 40% (or 60% for long-production/aircraft) in lieu of 100% for the first year ending after Jan 19, 2025. 2026 default 100%.

obbba_statute_2026.title: OBBBA personal deductions (Pub. L. 119-21) — IRC 151(d)(5)(C), 224, 225, 163(h)(4)
obbba_statute_2026.note: 2026 amounts are identical to 2025: none of the four OBBBA personal deductions (senior bonus IRC 151(d)(5)(C); tips IRC 224; overtime IRC 225; car-loan interest IRC 163(h)(4)) are indexed for inflation. Senior bonus $6,000 (6% phase-out over $75,000 single / $150,000 MFJ); tips $25,000 ($150,000/$300,000, $100 per $1,000 rounded down); overtime $12,500/$25,000 (same phase-out); car-loan interest $10,000 ($100,000/$200,000, $200 per $1,000 rounded up). Effective 2025-2028. Confirmed non-indexed in statute text. OBBBA §70105 also widened the §199A(b)(3)(B) phase-in range to $75,000 (single/HoH/MFS) / $150,000 (MFJ) for TY after 12/31/2025 and added §199A(i): a $400 minimum deduction for an 'applicable taxpayer' with ≥$1,000 aggregate QBI from active (material-participation) trades/businesses; the $400 is the GREATER of the normal deduction or $400 and overrides the §199A(a)(2) overall taxable-income limit.

obbba_amt_2026.title: OBBBA AMT (Pub. L. 119-21 §70107) — IRC 55(d) phase-out reset for TY after 12/31/2025
obbba_amt_2026.note: OBBBA §70107 (Pub. L. 119-21, July 4 2025) made the TCJA AMT exemption/threshold increases permanent AND, for taxable years beginning after 12/31/2025: (a) reset the exemption phase-out threshold to $1,000,000 MFJ / $500,000 other (non-indexed through 2026 per §55(d)(4)(A)(ii)(I)); (b) doubled the phase-out rate from 25% to 50%, creating a steeper 'bump zone' (effective ~39%/42% within the phase-out range). The 28% breakpoint remains inflation-indexed via Rev. Proc. 2025-32 ($244,500 / $122,250 MFS — see rev_proc_2025_32_ty2026). 2026 exemptions 140,200 MFJ / 90,100 single / 70,100 MFS.

obbba_salt_2026.title: Pub. L. 119-21 §70120 / IRC 164(b)(6) and (b)(7) as amended — 2026 SALT cap & phase-down
obbba_salt_2026.quote: IRC 164(b)(7)(A) applicable limitation amount: '(ii) in the case of any taxable year beginning in calendar year 2026, $40,400'; '(iii) in the case of any taxable year beginning after calendar year 2026 and before 2030, 101 percent of the dollar amount in effect under this subparagraph for taxable years beginning in the preceding calendar year'. IRC 164(b)(6)(B): 'the applicable limitation amount (half the applicable limitation amount in the case of a married individual filing a separate return)'. IRC 164(b)(7)(B)(i): 'the applicable limitation amount shall be reduced by 30 percent of the excess (if any) of the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income over the threshold amount (half the threshold amount in the case of a married individual filing a separate return)'. IRC 164(b)(7)(B)(ii): '(I) in the case of any taxable year beginning in calendar year 2025, $500,000'; '(II) in the case of any taxable year beginning in calendar year 2026, $505,000'; '(III) in the case of any taxable year beginning after calendar year 2026, 101 percent of the dollar amount in effect under this subparagraph for taxable years beginning in the preceding calendar year'. IRC 164(b)(7)(B)(iii): 'The reduction under clause (i) shall not result in the applicable limitation amount being less than $10,000.'
obbba_salt_2026.note: Resolves the two conflicts secondary sources had (plan E1): (1) the MFS cap ESCALATES — 'half the applicable limitation amount' — so 2026 MFS cap = $20,200, not the frozen $20,000 one secondary source claimed; (2) the 2026 phase-down MAGI start is $505,000 (101% of the 2025 $500,000 threshold), not the $500,500 another source gave. Both the cap and the threshold escalate at 101%/year through 2029; after 2029 the cap drops to $10,000. The $10,000 reduction floor is stated without a 'half' qualifier in (b)(7)(B)(iii); the existing 2026 salt.floor_mfs = 5000 follows the 'half' rule of (b)(6)(B) and the established 2025 pattern. Source hierarchy attempted in order: govinfo.gov PLAW-119publ21 (truncated, body did not reach §70120); uscode.house.gov (returned the 2000 edition, pre-SALT); Cornell LII (current-law text, succeeded — used here).

irc_408d8_qcd.title: IRC 408(d)(8) — Qualified Charitable Distribution limit (pre-2024 statutory)
irc_408d8_qcd.note: $100,000 aggregate annual QCD limit, fixed by statute 2016-2023. SECURE 2.0 Act section 112 (Pub. L. 117-328, Div. T) added inflation indexing beginning 2024 (Notice 2023-75 raised it to $105,000).

usc_199a_qbi_statute.title: 26 USC 199A — Qualified business income (as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §§70105, 70201(d))
usc_199a_qbi_statute.note: §199A(a): deduction = lesser of combined QBI amount or 20% of (taxable income − net capital gain); amended 'except as provided in subsection (i)'. §199A(b)(1)(A)/(c): 20% QBI rate and 20% REIT/PTP rate. §199A(b)(2)(B): W-2 wage/UBIA limit = greater of 50% of W-2 wages or 25% of W-2 wages + 2.5% of UBIA. §199A(e)(3): net capital gain per §1(h)(11) includes qualified dividends. §199A(i)(1): for an 'applicable taxpayer' (aggregate QBI from active—materially-participated—trades/businesses ≥ $1,000 per §199A(i)(2)), deduction = GREATER of the normally-computed deduction or $400; this OVERRIDES the §199A(a)(2) overall taxable-income limit. $400/$1,000 fixed for 2026, inflation-adjusted (nearest $5) for TY after 2026.

irs_form_8995a_instructions.title: Instructions for Form 8995-A (2025) — QBI Deduction
irs_form_8995a_instructions.note: Part II lines 4-11: line 5 = 50% of W-2 wages; line 6 = 25% of W-2 wages; line 8 = 2.5% of UBIA; line 10 = greater of line 5 or (line 6 + line 8); line 11 = lesser of 20% of QBI or line 10. SSTB list (Reg §1.199A-5): health, law, accounting, consulting, financial services, performing arts, athletics, and the 'principal asset is the reputation or skill' catch-all. The tool ASKS the user for SSTB status rather than inferring it.

fbar._note: FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR). Deliberately NOT under a tax-year block: the reporting threshold and the recordkeeping period are statutory and un-indexed, the deadline is a fixed month/day of the following year, and the penalty maxima are indexed by the year the penalty is ASSESSED, not by the tax year reported on. See references/fbar_guide.md.
